novelty_signal: Promote. The probe says composite packets are the missing abstraction, and the benchmark report says the repo still lacks the actuator-basis ablation needed to tell a bad CA rule from a bad one-packet basis.
validation_plan: Enumerate symmetry-safe 2-packet, 4-packet, and run-boundary composites on the canonical 64-modular seed and at least one harder synthetic control.
Compute exact delta fingerprints and retain only packets with sharply reduced changed-lag support plus neutral or improving frontier behavior.
Benchmark full CA, scorer-only, greedy, tabu, and simulated annealing on the same retained library and budget.
Track changed-lag footprint, touched-edge count, packet scan width, exact-hit rate, and seed-improvement rate so locality and performance are measured together.
risk: The gain may come entirely from the new packet basis and help every baseline equally, leaving little CA-specific value.
Composite packets can quietly smuggle in known structure or expand toward whole-state search.
A useful low-splash library may simply not exist at the canonical seed.

bridge: Derived defect-packet influence graph / LDPC-style graph CA
novelty_signal: Promote. The probe says honest locality lives on a derived influence graph rather than on raw q/s adjacency, and that claim is compatible with the verifier's fake-locality diagnosis.
validation_plan: Build a sparse bipartite defect-packet graph from exact delta tables of the retained packet library.
Run weighted bit-flip, local-auction graph CA, and scorer-only ablations under the same graph, seed, and evaluation budget.
Instrument neighborhood size, message count, active-node count, and dependence on global rescoring.
Reject the bridge if useful trajectories require dense scans, dense collective flips, or family leakage.
risk: The graph may be only a sparse view of globally scored search rather than a genuine local dynamic.
Sparsification may erase the real defect geometry and act only as a preconditioner.
The graph construction can still encode known structured-family constraints.

bridge: Lag-residue CA on four 167-channels with family-leakage audit
novelty_signal: Hold. H2 remains the cleanest backup branch, but the latest verification summary says the pivot-to-H2 story is still interpretation and H2 stays blocked until a family-leakage artifact exists.
validation_plan: Implement one lag-residue representation with an exact map back to q/s or sequence-space edits.
Run one matched non-CA lag-space control before any broader sweep.
Execute the Williamson, Turyn, Goethals-Seidel, cocyclic, and block-circulant leakage audit as a saved artifact.
Promote only if the branch beats basis-only and graph-only controls without whole-spectrum rescans.
risk: The branch can collapse into optimizer-over-known-family.
Lag-locality may still be fake once moves are projected back to actual edits.
The bridge may be unnecessary if the packet-library plus influence-graph path already explains the failure.

bridge: Warning-propagation or lag-field side channels on the same local graph
novelty_signal: Hold. The autocorrelation landscape makes field channels attractive, but the verifier says they must remain side information and must beat matched non-CA use to support a CA-specific claim.
validation_plan: Compute warning-propagation or lag-field summaries on the same retained library and influence graph.
Compare graph CA alone, field-guided non-CA search, and the hybrid under identical accounting.
Measure reversal rate, vote coherence, active-neighborhood size, and exact-hit or seed-improvement outcomes.
Reject the bridge if the same fields help non-CA methods equally or if they rely on global information.
risk: The method can collapse into message passing with a thin CA wrapper.
Field channels may simply act as global scoring features in disguise.
A hybrid gain may still belong to feature engineering rather than CA dynamics.

novelty_signal: Hold. Controlled worsening bursts are probably necessary because monotone local descent is dead on the canonical seed, but schedule claims are premature until the actuator basis and locality mechanism are isolated.
validation_plan: Test local burst schedules only on the retained low-splash packet library or influence graph scaffold.
Compare fixed local scheduling, adaptive criticality, and matched annealing-style controls under the same action set.
Count burst size, burst duration, neighborhood radius, and dependence on any global temperature or full scan.
Promote only if barrier crossing stays spatially bounded and improves lexicographic objective relative to the same basis without the schedule.
risk: The schedule can degenerate into annealing written in local language.
Useful bursts may require neighborhoods large enough to destroy the locality claim.
Schedule tuning can waste budget before the representation problem is solved.

bridge: Current single-packet defect-syndrome CA on the q/s packet lattice
novelty_signal: Retire. The matched frontier batch, the probe, and the verification pack all agree that this branch is frozen, fake-local, and no longer defensible as an active search direction.
validation_plan: Keep it only as a negative control for future actuator-basis and locality ablations.
Reuse its diagnostics, especially support diffusion, packet splash, and frontier freeze, as baseline failure signatures.
risk: No improving one-packet or two-packet moves were found on the canonical seed.
All recorded frontier restarts exceeded the seed support without improving the seed objective.
Further tuning risks rebranding globally scored local search as CA.
